title: Egyptian Nabonassar Era Calendar
intro: The Egyptian Nabonassar Era is an ancient-style wandering civil year used as a chronological and astronomical reference.
epoch: 1 Thoth, year 1 corresponds to 26 February 747 BCE in Julian reckoning (JDN 1448638).
structure: Twelve 30-day months form 360 days. Five additional days follow Mesore, producing exactly 365 days every year; no leap day is inserted.
example: After Mesore 30 come the five extra days. The next day is 1 Thoth of the following year.
history: Because the seasonal solar year is slightly longer than the Egyptian civil year, the calendar gradually wanders through the seasons. The Nabonassar era provided a later astronomical chronological reference.
model: For arithmetic year y, month m and day d, JDN = 1448638+365*(y-1)+30*(m-1)+d-1. Month 13 allows only days 1–5. The inverse uses floor division of JDN-1448638 by 365, with a nonnegative remainder giving the day within the year. Signed day-coordinate extremes must be rejected if conversion cannot round-trip.
limits: This is Ptolemaic-era Nabonassar reckoning, not the later Coptic leap-year calendar or a reconstruction of all pharaonic regnal dates.
